note: The system's nouns (EE-014). Standards first: a noun uses an established term with its standard meaning, and is coined only when none exists ('ours'). Each noun names its function (one id from operations/departments.json, or null when the word is shared). A null noun may appear in any package and never decides the package's type. handoff_type is true when the noun can type a handoff package. A function is a noun at level function, and its capabilities are the nouns it owns. Retired nouns list what replaced them; schema/check-nouns.mjs fails when one reappears in the checked files. References are ids in <layer>/references/references.json.

nouns.meaning: The name of the system
How files refer to the whole. Proposed genus (EE-024): a venture development framework; operating system and operating model are set aside

Proposed genus of the Everything Ecosystem (EE-024): an opinionated framework for developing ventures, in the same genus as web development frameworks. Like them it gives conventions over configuration (one default per choice, with references), a fixed structure the builder fills in (the venture folder, layers and records), generators (init-venture), checks that run like tests, a data model, and packages (packages/<name>/package.json, EE-071). The builder's venture calls on it, and its checks call back on the venture's records
nouns.standard: software framework (Johnson and Foote 1988; Rails' convention over configuration) applied to venture development (venture building, venture studios)

nouns.meaning: What a venture's scaffolding is (EE-085): one structure for everything the venture knows, under one set of conventions, with pointers to the systems of record that keep the rest. It suits solo founders and small founding teams, for whom one central structure replaces separate SaaS silos and gives agents the whole picture
What to do: Product Anatomy, handoffs; MAD, the method for building software, is a separate product (EE-038)
What to record: venture.json, products, decisions, references
What helps do it: scripts, skills, agent rules
One builder's instance of the system, declared by workspace.json

One of the six: purpose, knowledge, operations, evidence, governance, interface (execution folded into operations, EE-038). A layer organizes the framework repository (its manifest is <layer>/layer.json). It is a property of a record type, not a venture folder (EE-071)
The unit: anything a builder undertakes, from a hobby to a company. Ventures can hold ventures
How far a venture has come: discovery, validation, beachhead, scale, platform
The test for leaving a phase: problem-solution fit, product-market fit (retention), repeatability, market leadership
Why the venture exists and how far it means to go: hobby, survival, lifestyle, managed growth, aggressive growth
none, sole-prop, partnership, llc, s-corp, c-corp, benefit-corp, nonprofit
bootstrapped, grant, angel, venture capital, debt, mixed
What the venture produces, by its current flagship
The promise, who it is made to, what it must not deliver, and the competence behind it

Was the record for a party a venture serves; not universal, since many ventures have customers, users, members or an audience instead. Now a value of an account's relationship (served under a professional relationship)

A named party a venture keeps a record for, at accounts/<id>/account.json, with a relationship: client, customer, user, member, partner or other. Optional; who a product serves in general is its market

How a party or market stands to the venture: customer (buys), client (served under a professional relationship), user (uses, may not pay), member (belongs), audience (reads, watches or listens; markets only), partner
nouns.standard: common business usage; client as a customer of professional services

nouns.meaning: What crosses from one venture into another, one way, with a border
The readable companion to venture.json: narrative, pillars, changelog

A business function with one accountable owner. One person may own several. A solo founder owns them all. Decision rights and the team plan point at function owners (EE-071). department is the alias for one release
Product, brand and business, in every venture
The scaffold for a venture: pillars, roles, decision rights
One thing a venture offers, stored as a card in products/
Who a product serves: customer type, segment, geography, vertical or horizontal
The need a product meets
nouns.standard: Abell (customer functions); jobs to be done

nouns.meaning: How a product meets the need
product, service, platform, content, marketplace
How a product earns, by St. Gallen pattern names
A product's place in each phase: flagship, substrate, revenue engine, wedge, option, end product
A portfolio role: the narrow product or segment used to enter a market
The method that judges products against the core product
Part of Product Anatomy that assigns portfolio roles by phase
A logged choice with an id (EE- or a venture's own prefix)
A source behind a default, recorded per layer with a stance
One of MAD's four levels: governance, delivery, software engineering, automation; MAD is a separate product, and Mentura records name a tier only where a venture uses MAD (EE-038)
One unit of delegated work: a JSON record (role, decision classes, done-criteria, status, attempts) at <venture>/operations/handoffs/<id>.json with a Markdown brief beside it
One check that says a handoff is finished: conformance (a command, no model, no reviewer), self-proof (the change exercised for real, with output) or review (fit to intent, by a named role)
A test of whether something worked; evals are grouped in eval suites (eval-suite.schema.json)
The recorded result of one run of a check or eval: subject and version, each criterion's outcome and its output, at <venture>/evidence/results/<id>.json. Append-only
A person's or agent's job; never a product's place in the portfolio
Who the venture needs, agent or person, by phase, with the authority each holds and where a human stays in the loop; recruiting briefs for open person roles (operations/team-plan.json, EE-029)
The person who decides, reviews or does the part of a task that agents cannot, may not, or are not known to do; named for every such agent task
What agents can, cannot, may not or are not yet known to do, task by task, with sources and dates, fed by research and our own evals (evidence/capabilities/agent-capabilities.json, EE-029)
Who may decide what, at one of four levels: decide, decide-inform, recommend-approve, escalate. A venture may tighten the template, never loosen it without a named decision
A custom workbench built for the system: a viewer over a venture's records

A tool through which a person, with agents, works across all or most other layers at once in one session (reaches at least four of the six). A tool that serves one or two layers is an integration of those layers, however good its screen is. Renamed from "harness" (EE-096), which was renamed from "interface" (EE-093)
nouns.standard: workbench (Eclipse Platform Workbench; Fowler, language workbench), narrowed

nouns.meaning: The software around a model that runs it: it gives the model its context and tools and carries out what the model asks (the Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, Claude Code). AI harness and agent harness are kinds of harness. A harness needs no person (the Agent SDK); one a person works through across most layers is also a workbench (EE-096)
nouns.standard: harness (industry usage; Anthropic S-1, 2026); workspace rule G-039

nouns.meaning: An AI harness in which the model directs its own steps and tool use in a loop toward a goal, acting on files, tools and systems between the person's turns, under permissions (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Hermes Agent). Every agent harness is an AI harness; a chatbot is not an agent harness. One a person uses across at least four layers is also a workbench
A product that is the software around a model: the person's work happens in exchanges with it, so without the model nothing is left. A chatbot is one. The model answers; the person acts
A model used inside a product that does its job without it (summaries, search, drafting). Test: remove the model and the product still works. Most apps that implement AI are here, not harnesses
A workbench built for the system or a venture rather than bought, such as the operator console. Was "custom interface" (EE-093), then "custom harness" (EE-096)

A tool or service one layer uses, listed in <layer>/tooling/integrations.json (Obsidian for knowledge, Linear for operations, GitHub checks for evidence). A workbench reaches integrations; it is not one

Mentura's word (EE-071): an enhanced package that adds automations, agent workflows, richer skills and connectors, at platform/kits/<name>/kit.json. A kit names the one package it extends and never replaces it, so the package works without the kit. The framework does not use kit for its own manifests (was the layer bundle at <layer>/kit.json)
nouns.standard: product bundling (Adams and Yellen 1976), kept for the platform

nouns.meaning: Old name for the unit
Old formation stage (hobby, venture, company)
Old sphere kinds (venture, client)
Old first market phase
Old scale phase
Old last phase
The old name for the venture profile
Old name of the venture template
Proposed for-profit/nonprofit axis, dropped before use

The list of every record type in the ecosystem, the layer that owns it, its schema, where its records live and what it references (schema/data-model.json). It is the master map; no single schema contains everything
One kind of record in the data model, such as venture, product, handoff or evidence, owned by exactly one layer or by the system

The file (<layer>/layer.json, system layer at schema/layer.json) that lists what one layer of the framework repository holds: its skills, the record types it still owns, those it reads and writes, and its checks. Layer relationships are derived from manifests (EE-018, EE-071)

The folder of documents (Markdown notes and JSON records) that holds a workspace's venture folders, their records and decisions. Every workspace has one; a venture outside software may need nothing else
nouns.standard: Obsidian's name for a folder of notes; generically a knowledge base

nouns.meaning: A version-controlled store, normally Git, holding code and the documents that ship with it (docs-as-code). A venture that builds software needs at least one; repo is the short form
The record of who owns the venture and on what terms: share classes, holders, grants with vesting, the option pool, SAFEs and notes (governance/ownership.json)
nouns.standard: capitalization table (common startup and finance usage)

nouns.meaning: A kind of share (or LLC unit) with its own votes, price and rights: common, preferred, super-voting, non-voting
Earning granted shares over time, commonly four years with a one-year cliff, so that someone who leaves early keeps only what they earned
What founders agreed with each other: roles, commitment, IP assignment, departure and deadlock terms; required once two or more founders share ownership
A formal board of directors (or managers, or trustees), which holds legal authority, or an advisory board, which advises and decides nothing (governance/board.json)
nouns.standard: corporate law; Feld and Ramsinghani, Startup Boards

nouns.meaning: A decision only the formal board may make, such as issuing shares or selling the company
A right an investor gets with a class or instrument: board seat, information, pro-rata, protective provisions, anti-dilution, drag-along, tag-along, right of first refusal and others
The order and amounts in which sale proceeds reach each owner. Retired here because waterfall is a delivery methodology in MAD's delivery tier
How owners realize value or the venture ends: acquisition, IPO, secondary sale, merger, management buyout, wind-down, or hold (governance/exit.json)
The order and amounts in which a sale's proceeds reach each owner, preferences first by seniority, then common; computed from the cap table by schema/payouts.mjs, never typed
nouns.standard: venture finance usage (pref stack; Feld and Mendelson, Venture Deals)

nouns.meaning: Where a venture publishes and who may publish what there: its channels, the guidelines each follows, the checks and preview every publication passes, and who drafts and approves by role or team (governance/publication-policy.json, EE-025)
nouns.standard: content governance; communications or disclosure policy (corporate usage)

nouns.meaning: A place the venture publishes to (website, docs site, social account, newsletter, app store, press, investor update, regulatory filing); its destination decides which guidelines apply
One act of making something public on a channel; always a handoff under the public-commitment decision class, previewed, checked and approved by a person
The rules for using the venture's visual and verbal identity, kept by the brand pillar
nouns.standard: brand guidelines or brand book (common marketing usage)

nouns.meaning: What content covers and how it is written, separate from brand voice; a style guide is one part
nouns.standard: editorial guidelines and style guide (publishing usage)

nouns.meaning: The end a venture exists to reach (purpose/telos.json): statement, end state, measures, the owners' intended outcome, and exit criteria for each phase. Start with the end: other layers derive from it
nouns.standard: Aristotle (final cause); Covey, begin with the end in mind

nouns.meaning: What must be true for a venture to leave a phase, written in its telos and tied to a telos measure; it refines that phase's generic gate. Not an owner's exit (governance)
A fill-in starting point for one record or document: the fields, what to write in each and what a strong one looks like. A kit holds templates; a template holds no rules and checks nothing

The probability that a venture is validated: a weighted average of sub-scores (problem, solution, product-market fit, pricing, go-to-market, team, operations readiness), each a Jev probability times its evidence weight, with floors; replaces a declared phase gate (EE-026)

How much a validation record's cited evidence can be trusted: high, moderate, low or very low, from the kind of signal, the audience, the sample, the specificity and the age; a claim with no evidence is very low

The probability that a venture needs a record type in its current phase and the next, from priors raised or lowered by facts about the venture; records below 0.5 are held back unless the builder asks, so builders don't overbuild (EE-028)
nouns.standard: ours; just-in-time (lean manufacturing) and YAGNI (extreme programming) in spirit

nouns.meaning: A MAD answer taken from a venture's records (telos, ownership, board, form, decision rights) instead of asked again; it names the record it came from Retired with MAD's move out of Mentura (EE-038).

The address of one record type or command in a venture, such as purpose/validation/problem: a layer, then a kit when the record sits in a nested kit, then the record. Generated from the data model and kits; the CLI, the MCP server and the HTTP API share one route table (EE-030)
nouns.standard: routing in web frameworks (Next.js App Router, Rails routes)

nouns.meaning: A gated record an agent wrote, held in <venture>/_drafts/ until a person accepts it; the decision class of the record says it is a person's to make (EE-030)

Who or what produced a record, by which activity, from what, and under which decision: explicit in the provenance log for writes through the router, implicit in git history for everything else (EE-031)

A venture's append-only record of writes, <venture>/provenance.jsonl: one line per write naming the file, the activity (write, draft, accept, baseline), the person or agent and the interface, what it was derived from and the decision; each line carries the previous line's hash (EE-031)
nouns.standard: W3C PROV; hash-chained append-only log (common audit usage)

nouns.meaning: The context that wraps a route: the system, layer and kit purpose, skills and references, the template, the gate and what need-now says, given to an agent before it acts on the route (EE-032)
A route rendered as a page for a person; the Markdown form of a record or command result. The operator console will render views (EE-032)
A named set of routes that shares a layout without changing their paths; one per phase, (discovery) to (platform), holding the routes need-now suggests in that phase (EE-032)
One part of a page that renders on its own beside others, such as @validation in the venture overview; a slot that fails shows its error while the rest render (EE-032)
An old route kept after a rename, which the router follows to the new one with a deprecation note (EE-032)

The records a founder keeps in front of them every day until they are muscle memory, answering why, what, who, how, when, where and whether, with brand beside them (purpose/strategic-foundation.json). Each foundation statement is an attribute of an existing record; changing one is deliberate (type to confirm) and confirmed statements unlock delegation (EE-051, EE-052)
nouns.standard: strategic foundation in strategic planning (mission, vision, values), widened by the Five Ws and How

nouns.meaning: Retired for strategic foundation and foundation statement (EE-052)
The function that sets the venture's direction: vision, and the choices that follow from it. A solo founder holds it with the others.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 1.0 Develop Vision and Strategy

nouns.meaning: The function that develops what the venture offers, and the decisions that change the offering.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 2.0 Develop and Manage Products and Services

nouns.meaning: The function that finds the buyer and sells the offering, including the price.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services

nouns.meaning: The function that keeps the books: revenue, cost, and the customer as an account.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 9.0 Manage Financial Resources

nouns.meaning: The buyer this function sells to. The finance sense of the same word is customer@finance. The @ scope is the one the term list uses for two senses of one word.
The party the books record as the source of revenue. The marketing sense of the same word is customer@marketing-and-sales.
A decision that sets or approves a price. Marketing and sales owns the decision. Every package of this type lists finance in touches, and the founder approves.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 3.2.2 Define pricing strategy, including 3.2.2.4 Approve pricing strategy

nouns.meaning: A decision that changes what the venture offers. The products function owns it.
nouns.standard: APQC PCF 7.4 Cross-Industry 2.0 Develop and Manage Products and Services

nouns.meaning: A package typed by the founder term (schema/terms, EE-095). Its facts are that term's properties, and the membership gate runs those checks. Strategy holds the type while human capital is not an active function.
